content.text:
Implement the agreed Tailor proof of concept in https://github.com/nitink133/tailor-neathack. Use Fable 5.1 as the orchestrator and coordinate a parallel team of coding agents.
SOURCE OF TRUTH
Read Linear NIT-269 and all its children:
- NIT-270: Neatlogs adapter knowledge and tool contracts.
- NIT-273: Isolated personalised demo data and session tools.
- NIT-272: Server-side agent and buyer chat integration.
- NIT-271: Independent tests and evidence.
Parent: https://linear.app/nitinkhanna/issue/NIT-269/build-personalised-tailor-agent-proof
Workshop: [Tailor product and proof workshop](https://chatgpt.com/space/page_a57ae2efb9808191ab50b99c369d35cf)
Read AGENTS.md, the project-local Entire skill and existing handoff/audit documents. Verify the starting revision includes origin/main commit bbb2600a001c5ae8c7e364c754dae77ca7b186dc or a verified successor. Inspect the current code rather than assuming ticket descriptions prove functionality. Preserve existing changes and reuse completed work.
TEAM AND EXECUTION
Use actual models available in Cursor. Assign strong reasoning models to architecture, contracts, security and independent review; strong coding models to backend and agent/UI work; faster capable models to structured extraction and straightforward tests. Report actual assignments. If Fable 5.1 or mixed-model parallel execution is unavailable, explain the limitation rather than claiming it ran.
NIT-270 should publish a small shared contract snapshot first. Then run backend/session work and agent/UI work in parallel. QA can design tests immediately and run integration tests as code arrives. Continue broader product research alongside implementation; don’t wait for an exhaustive catalogue to start.
Give each worker explicit file ownership. Coordinate shared schemas and routes through one integration owner. Reuse an existing isolated worktree where appropriate; avoid nested duplicate worktrees. Use separate feature branches/worktrees when workers need isolation. Don’t modify main directly, merge into main, force-push, amend history or deploy.
PRODUCT OUTCOME
Tailor helps an anonymous buyer understand how Neatlogs could help their project through a personalised synthetic demo. It is more than a chatbot describing features.
Example acceptance journey:
A buyer says, “I’m building a travel-booking agent. Show me a booking API timeout followed by a successful retry.” Tailor prepares a coherent fictional trace visible in the existing Neatlogs-style UI. The buyer then says, “Make the retry fail too.” Tailor updates that session’s scenario, verifies the saved spans and explains the resulting failure and escalation.
Current code has a working UI, SQLite state and two fixed fixtures selected by keyword matching. It does not yet establish a live agent or a source-backed vendor knowledge layer. Extend it without rebuilding the clone.
ARCHITECTURE
- One server-side product agent. The coding swarm does not imply a multi-agent product runtime.
- Versioned repository files for Neatlogs product knowledge, capability definitions and tool contracts. No new memory vendor or vector database for this slice.
- SQLite for active anonymous buyer conversations and authoritative demo state.
- Load relevant knowledge, conversation context and current scenario version for each turn.
- The model interprets requests, asks clarifications, proposes bounded actions and explains verified results.
- Deterministic code enforces permissions, schemas, relationships, timing consistency, session ownership and version checks.
- Save transactionally, read back independently and only then claim the change succeeded.
ADAPTER KNOWLEDGE
Reuse existing research and verify important claims against official Neatlogs documentation and pricing. Each capability record should include the buyer problem, feature behaviour, limitations, prerequisites, plan availability, source URL/date, example questions, demonstration evidence and available tools.
Separate official product capabilities from clone capabilities. Record whether each feature can be explained, demonstrated, modified or is unsupported. Unknown pricing or entitlements must remain unknown; hackathon access is not proof of ordinary plan availability.
Begin executable coverage with traces, spans, failures, retries and outcomes. Keep the format extensible to broader offerings. Don’t silently expand into cloning every Neatlogs feature.
TOOLS AND DATA
Replace exact-fixture-only validation with bounded personalised synthetic data. Allow fictional names, workflow steps, tool-call examples, retry outcomes, errors and coherent timings. Preserve consistent trace/span relationships and cross-view totals.
Never allow arbitrary code execution, real Neatlogs product mutations, cross-buyer access or fabricated product features/pricing. Harmless changes within the buyer’s own synthetic session don’t need a confirmation click each time.
Handle save-success/readback-failure accurately. Don’t say the old scenario is unchanged unless verified. Fix transcript concurrency and message-limit handling. Explanations must use the actual selected trace/span evidence, not merely the fixture name.
BUYER EXPERIENCE AND MEMORY
Preserve the Neatlogs-styled chat entry and persistent side panel. Include clear “Powered by Tailor” attribution. Keep internal adapter jargon out of buyer-facing copy without pretending that mock-backed behaviour is live AI.
When a material detail is unclear, ask one short question with three relevant choices and optional free text. Don’t force a company-name questionnaire or ask unnecessary questions.
Implement anonymous session-only memory: 60 minutes of inactivity, a maximum lifetime of 4 hours and an explicit End demo action. Reload works within an active session. Expiry removes access and deletes the session’s conversation/demo content. Do not recognise returning buyers across visits. Longer-term vendor analytics is outside this slice.
MODEL AND COST GATES
Build a provider abstraction and use a mock provider initially. Exact live provider/model, API eligibility, permitted data flow and testing budget are not approved yet. Don’t make live model calls, incur charges, create/configure credentials or send buyer content externally without my approval.
Missing credits must not block contracts, validators, session logic or mocked integration. Start with one capable live model when later approved. Keep validation and persistence model-free. Stronger-model escalation must be bounded; cheaper-model routing can follow evaluation rather than adding complexity immediately.
NEATLOGS RUNTIME OBSERVABILITY
This is required implementation scope. Reuse the existing Neatlogs SDK/configuration and verify its official contract. Don’t invent endpoints or attributes.
Instrument actual Tailor turns and relevant retrieval, model, tool, validation, save, readback and response steps. Capture clarification, refusal, retries and failures with safe correlation IDs, real latency and provider-reported usage where available. Never present estimated or missing tokens as measured values.
Keep these separate:
- Synthetic traces in the replica demonstrate the buyer’s fictional workflow.
- Real Tailor telemetry goes to the configured Tailor Neatlogs project, not the demo sandbox.
Redact before export. Don’t log credentials, raw buyer conversations or full model/tool payloads by default. Bound telemetry retries/buffers and prevent exporter failures from breaking the demo. Remote telemetry retention is separate from SQLite session deletion and needs an explicit policy.
Backend owns exporter plumbing and tool/persistence spans; agent/UI owns turn/model/retrieval spans; QA verifies correlation, redaction and failure paths. Avoid duplicate instrumentation.
Test with a local captured/mock exporter first. Keep external ingestion verification pending until the destination and safe payload are confirmed and I approve the run. Distinguish instrumentation implemented, local tests passed, trace actually visible in Neatlogs, and real-model execution verified. SDK send success alone is not dashboard evidence. Label mock-backed execution honestly.
ENTIRE DEVELOPMENT RECORDING
Follow the project-local Entire skill for each supported coding session. Preserve existing checkpoints and verify normal hook-based sync when pushing. Don’t fabricate trailers or treat the known Analytics display discrepancy as capture proof or failure. Report genuine capture gaps separately from Git publication.
TESTS AND DELIVERY
Independent QA must cover unfamiliar buyer wording, personalised scenario creation, follow-up changes, three-option clarification, saved-evidence explanations, navigation/reload, session isolation/expiry, concurrent updates, unsupported and prompt-injection requests, tool failure and truthful recovery. Use injected clocks where appropriate to test expiry without waiting hours.
Run applicable type checks, build, automated and browser tests against the integrated feature branch. Report passed, failed and unrun checks separately. No live-provider or telemetry acceptance claim without actual authorised evidence.
Update Linear with concise progress, blockers, commit links and evidence. Update handoff documentation with what works, what is mock-backed and what still needs approval. Commit and push scoped feature branches normally, verifying remote SHAs and checkpoint refs. Leave main merges and deployment for my approval.
Start by posting a concise ownership/dependency plan, then execute NIT-270’s minimal contract milestone and the parallel implementation lanes. Don’t stop after planning. Escalate decisions that materially change scope, safety, cost or shared contracts.

content.text:
The preflight confirms the orchestrator session is active on main in the primary checkout, with fresh lifecycle evidence. Since I can't modify main directly, I need to set up a feature branch for the workers to use instead.

Since the checkout is clean, creating and checking out a feature branch from main here seems fine—"don't modify main directly" just means not committing to main itself. The alternative is reusing the existing isolated worktree already on the target feature branch, but since Task-launched subagents run in the same local workspace as the primary checkout, their edits would land there regardless of which branch I check out.

Given disjoint file ownership across workers, isolation via separate worktrees isn't strictly needed — I can run everyone in this single checkout on one integration branch, with me as orchestrator handling commits and Entire trailers. I'll leave the separate orchestrator worktree alone since it's on a different branch. I should still fetch origin to confirm the commit hash matches origin/main's head, though I need to check whether that read-only fetch is permitted under the preflight rules.

Since the user explicitly asked me to verify origin/main's commit, fetching is authorized; I'll use a lightweight `git ls-remote origin main` instead of a full fetch to keep it minimal. Now I'm checking which models are available in this session, confirming I'm running as the orchestrator model and noting the other models present for delegation.

The user explicitly requested assigning strong reasoning models to architecture/contracts/security/review, strong coding models to backend/agent/UI, and faster models to extraction/tests, which authorizes me to pick specific model slugs and report the assignments. I'm starting to map NIT-270's contract work to a strong reasoning model, though I'm also considering handling it myself as orchestrator since I already have context on the codebase.

For accuracy I'll go with gpt-5.6-sol-medium for the knowledge lane since it balances speed and reliability against fabrication risks. So lane A is the contract snapshot (me), lane B is knowledge package via subagent with web research, and now I'm mapping out lane C for the backend/session/validator work needing a strong coding subagent.

For C, since the backend involves SQLite, transactions, expiry logic, and concurrency concerns, I'll assign claude-opus-5-5-medium given its intricacy. For D, the agent/UI work, claude-sonnet-5-5-high should handle it well. For E, QA tests need to be designed against the contract before code lands — I'll use a faster model like gemini-3.8-flash-high or composer-2.5-fast for scaffolding, then bring in a strong model for independent review at the end.

I also need to settle ownership for telemetry: backend owns the exporter plumbing and span helpers in a shared module, while the agent lane just consumes that helper API, so I'll define the interface upfront in the contract to avoid blocking. Similarly, the server route for handling chat turns lives in backend's server.ts but calls into the agent module's handler, so I need to pin down that handler's interface in the contract snapshot too.

A real risk here is parallel subagents sharing the same checkout — if one lane's files are mid-edit and broken, the other lane's typecheck will fail even on unrelated code. I'm thinking through mitigations: scoping typecheck errors to each lane's own files, or giving each lane a separate worktree to isolate changes entirely.

Worktrees would be cleaner for these two code lanes, but I need to check how session tracking interacts with that — since git hooks live in the shared `.git/hooks` directory across worktrees, commits in any worktree would trigger the same hooks, so checkpoint capture should still work even if subagents edit in separate worktrees.

Given the complexity, the simplest robust approach is probably a single checkout with disjoint file ownership between lanes, where lanes report typecheck failures outside their files rather than fixing them, and run only their specific test files with the test runner to avoid breaking each other's runs.

I should also flag the erasableSyntaxOnly constraint on tsc (no enums, no parameter properties) as something lanes need to follow, and figure out who owns tsconfig.browser.json since the client build only includes a few specific files — probably the agent/UI lane since it governs the browser build. Let me also check what's already sitting in the existing worktree to see if it can be reused.

As for the Codex worktree on the replica-app branch — since the primary checkout is clean on main and this capture is confirmed there, I'll create the feature branch directly in the primary checkout rather than nesting another worktree, as long as I'm not touching main itself.

I'll name the integration branch after the Linear ticket, something like `work/nit-269-build-personalised-tailor-agent-proof`. Other worktrees still reference their own branches independently, so switching the primary checkout off main shouldn't disrupt anything. Before proceeding I want to verify origin/main's head, check the orchestrator worktree log, skim the design docs for context, confirm node_modules and npm setup, then run typecheck and tests.

I also want to check the neatlogs SDK's type definitions for its telemetry contract, and do a bounded inspection of the session logs by grepping the session id in the entire.log tail to confirm the current session state without touching exited sessions.


Preflight checks pass so far—Entire CLI, session, and model all confirmed. Next I'll verify the remote baseline, SDK surface, and baseline checks before planning.

content.text:
I'm weighing whether importing the transitive OpenTelemetry dependency directly is fragile, versus having the backend tests use a caller-owned tracer provider with an in-memory exporter, and considering if adding it as an explicit devDependency is worth the package.json/lockfile churn.

minor decision I can just make myself — no package.json change, use the transitive import and document it.

Now I'll set up the branch: create `work/nit-269-build-personalised-tailor-agent-proof` off main in the primary checkout, write the contract snapshot, then post the plan to Linear before launching the lanes. Since the instructions were to post the ownership/dependency plan first, then execute the minimal contract milestone and parallel lanes, I'll design that plan now, starting with a single integration branch checked out in the primary workspace from `bbb2600`, since the live capture and subagent file edits all need to be verified in that exact session.

This keeps things simple — disjoint file ownership means isolation worktrees aren't needed, and no nested worktrees are required. Commits happen per lane milestone by the orchestrator with normal hooks, and the feature branch gets pushed at the end as authorized.

I'm second-guessing whether "scoped feature branches" plural implies the user wants separate branches per lane rather than one shared branch with lane-scoped commits — but since two branches can't be checked out in a single worktree, I'll keep to one integration branch with clearly scoped commits per lane and report this choice explicitly, since true isolation would require separate worktrees per lane.

Now I'm mapping out file ownership: as orchestrator handling the contracts work, I own the extension of the existing shared types file and need to create a new shared-seam types file defining the turn request/response envelope, the agent service and session tools interfaces, outcome states, limits config, clarification shape, and a telemetry helper interface. I'm also figuring out where versioned knowledge should live, leaning toward a dedicated knowledge directory with a capabilities file for things like Neatlogs.

I'm sketching the knowledge lane's ownership boundaries—it should own the knowledge directory, the typed loader, and its tests—while contracts defines the shared schema type. I'm also wrestling with who owns the deterministic validator for scenario proposals, since there's tension between which ticket assigns that responsibility, and I'm leaning toward having the contract itself define the validation rules.

Tests of examples against the real validator belong to QA/backend, not the contract itself. For backend NIT-273, I'm mapping out the files needed: server, store, fixtures, the new validator module, session tools, clock, telemetry exporter plumbing with redaction and bounded buffering, fixture scripts, and corresponding test files plus README updates. Then for the agent/UI piece under NIT-272, I'm starting to scope out its file list.

Continuing the file list for NIT-272, I'm noting it needs the new agent service, provider, mock provider, context, and prompts modules, plus the adapter (possibly retired), client, stylesheet, HTML entry point, browser tsconfig, and agent tests. I'm catching myself on ownership boundaries though—QA should own the new UI spec and qa-specific tests, while the agent lane just needs to keep the existing replica spec passing since the chat copy is changing.

Then for the knowledge NIT-270b branch, I'm mapping out its scope: the knowledge module itself, its test file, and the accompanying documentation on knowledge sources.

Moving to QA NIT-271, I'm deciding on model assignments—using a different strong-reasoning model for the independent review step so it's not the same model that authored the code, which keeps the review genuinely independent. That lane touches the qa test files, the new agent UI spec, and evidence/eval-set docs.

Now I'm sketching the actual seam design that ties all this together: a turn-submission endpoint that takes the user's text, a client-generated turn ID, an optional expected conversation version for optimistic concurrency, and an optional choice ID, returning a structured turn response. I'm also extending the session state to track conversation version, timing fields like expiry and last-active timestamps, the existing scenario version, an optional pending-clarification flag, and a "story" object holding the fictional project context used to ground the scenario.

I'm reworking the dataset model so it's keyed by a generic scenario slug rather than hardcoded values, replacing the old binary `recovered`/`exhausted` scenario type and its tied-together outcome and status fields with a more flexible `ScenarioKey` and a `label` field the UI can use generically instead of hardcoded conditionals.

This change ripples into the server-side filter validation, which needs to check against the dataset's actual scenario keys instead of a fixed union, and into the validator itself, which I'm swapping from exact-equality checks to a schema/coherence-based `validateProposal` that the existing fixtures still need to pass as a regression baseline.

Now I'm shaping the proposal contract itself — a `ScenarioProposal` carrying a contract version, expected dataset version for optimistic concurrency, a `basedOn` field distinguishing new scenarios from edits to existing traces, a fictional "story" context, and an array of up to four `ProposedTrace` entries with their labels, outcomes, and spans.

IDs are assigned deterministically from session and key rather than left to the model, preventing cross-session collisions. The validator enforces strict limits on count, string/JSON size, span hierarchy (single root, parent timing encloses child), and sane start/duration values.

I'm also reasoning through semantic consistency rules: error status must match a non-null error field, outcomeKind values like 'success' or 'failure' should align with whether any span actually errored, and root output should mirror the trace output. I'm weighing whether to reject strings resembling scripts or URLs, since realistic fictional tool calls might include URLs, but the requirement to avoid arbitrary executable content or links pushes me toward disallowing them outright.

de if missing, and auto-prefixes the trace name with 'SYNTHETIC ' when absent. For timing, I need child spans nested within parent durations while siblings can overlap for parallel calls, with ingestedAt stamped server-side rather than by the model. Now I'm defining the turn request/response envelope types, including fields like turnId, conversation and session versions, and an outcome enum covering answered, clarification, committed, rejected, and saved states.

I decide to rename the role to 'tailor' while still accepting 'adapter' for legacy session reads, and I expand statuses to include 'uncertain' and 'question'. Now I'm defining the SessionTools interface that the backend implements for the agent to call.

Defining session read and publish methods...

Now I'm sketching the agent service interface and the backend turn route: authorizing the session, locking against concurrent turns (returning 409 if one's already in flight), appending the buyer's message, invoking the agent, then appending the tailor's response and returning it.

I'm also defining the model provider interface, specifying how requests and responses are shaped including token usage and latency, plus the possible agent actions like asking a clarifying question, proposing something, or explaining with a citation.

For the mock provider, I'm designing it to be deterministic but generic: it should extract domain/workflow concepts from the buyer's own wording rather than relying on keyword fixtures, generating personalized proposals labeled clearly as heuristic mock output. I'm now sketching the limits configuration for session constraints.

I also need to resolve the 40-message cap inconsistency by making the server authoritative — keeping the last 120 turns, dropping oldest non-pinned turns when the cap is hit, and flagging the conversation as truncated so the UI can reflect that state accurately.

I'm defining a shared telemetry interface with `step` and `event` methods, which the backend implements using neatlogs tracing with redaction and a local exporter — the agent lane wraps model/retrieval steps, the backend wraps tool/save/readback steps, and the route wraps the whole turn as a workflow trace keyed by a hashed session ID and turn ID. Now I'm sketching the capability record schema, outlining fields like title, buyer problem, behavior, and limitations.

Completing more fields — prerequisites, plan availability, verified sources, demonstration evidence, and bounded topics — plus a separate pricing JSON file for unknowns, and a lightweight `selectKnowledge` loader that scores by keyword/topic rather than using a vector database.

Now I'm checking the `Scenario` type that both UI and server reference as a fixed union of `'recovered' | 'exhausted'`. Widening it to `string` is risky since other lanes' files depend on the strict union, but my contract snapshot just needs to typecheck against existing code at commit time — I'm verifying that fixtures and server checks still hold up if I generalize the type.

Widening to string works fine across adapter and client usages. Adding required `label` and `outcomeKind` fields to Trace will break fixtures.ts and tests, so rather than making them optional, I'll fix fixtures.ts myself as a small addition since I own the shared contract and need to keep the build green.

Now I'm thinking about what the knowledge lane needs to verify against official Neatlogs docs — likely neatlogs.com or docs.neatlogs.com. I'm not sure subagents have guaranteed MCP tool access, so I'll instruct them to use whatever web search/fetch tools are available and flag unverified claims otherwise. I should also account for the Linear attachments issue on NIT-269 where signed URLs expired after 5 minutes, meaning the old research attachments may no longer be accessible.

The existing research in the repo (docs/nit-265-reference.md) covers observed semantics, but the ChatGPT workshop page isn't accessible without auth, so I'll flag that too. Since there's no other existing documentation, my plan is to create a branch, use TodoWrite to track tasks, and post a concise ownership/dependency plan to Linear NIT-269 — since the user isn't watching live, Linear is the right place for that plan rather than the chat.

Next I'll write the contract files and commit them so the hooks capture the trailer, then verify the checkpoint before launching four subagents in parallel. I'm weighing whether to run them as background tasks — which means ending my turn and getting notified later, per the harness's notification pattern — versus running them blocking in a single message with multiple parallel Task calls, since background mode would surface an interim partial response to the user.

Running them blocking in parallel seems cleanest: a single message with multiple Task tool calls lets all four lanes execute simultaneously, and I just wait until all results return before integrating. The tradeoff is no mid-course coordination, but given the lane sizes, I'll go with blocking parallel calls and then run QA as a second wave after integration — though I'm still weighing whether QA should start earlier, designing tests against the contract before code lands, rather than only reviewing after.

I'll have wave 1 QA focus narrowly on things that don't depend on implementation details yet: eval sets, rubrics, test plans, and contract-level tests, while wave 2 QA runs the full suite against the actual integrated code and files defects back to the fix lanes via resume. The knowledge lane also runs in wave 1 alongside this. One concern I need to address is four subagents simultaneously modifying the same checkout and running test/build commands — I need to instruct each to scope their execution carefully to avoid collisions.

Each lane should only run its own test file plus a type-check, treat errors elsewhere as potentially transient and report rather than fix, and avoid git operations since the orchestrator handles commits. I'm also realizing the Playwright UI suite can't run concurrently across lanes due to shared port and sqlite file conflicts, so only the agent/UI lane runs it in wave 1 while QA runs it in wave 2, and the agent lane should use an alternate port for its dev server. Now I'll draft a concise plan comment for Linear, set up the contract, create the branch, and update the todo list before posting to Linear.


Baseline checks pass: main is in sync and clean, tests and typecheck are green, and the live session is confirmed active. Now I'll set up the integration branch and record the plan.

# NIT-269 contract snapshot `2026-10-11.1`

Owner: orchestrator (NIT-270). Frozen for the backend (NIT-273), agent/UI (NIT-272) and QA (NIT-271) lanes. Contract changes go through the orchestrator; lanes do not edit `src/contracts.ts`, `src/agent-contract.ts` or `src/examples/*` concurrently.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/contracts.ts` | Persisted data: `DemoSession`, `Dataset`, `Trace`, `Span`, `ChatTurn`, `Story`, `Clarification`, `Evidence`. Generalised from the two NIT-265 fixtures: `scenario` is any slug, traces carry `label` and `outcomeKind`. |
| `src/agent-contract.ts` | `LIMITS`, `ScenarioProposal`, `PublishResult`, `SessionTools`, `TurnRequest`/`TurnResponse`, `AgentService`, `ModelProvider`, `CapabilityRecord`/`KnowledgeIndex`, `TurnTelemetry`, `Clock`. |
| `src/examples/travel-booking.ts` | Travel-booking timeout → retry succeeds (v1, `mode: 'new'`), then "make the retry fail too" (v2, `mode: 'edit'`); refusal/unsupported/ambiguous request examples. |
| `test/contract.test.ts` | Model-free coherence checks over the examples and the regression fixtures. |

## Turn flow

```
POST /api/sessions/:id/turns  (owning cookie; body TurnRequest)
  server: authorise → lifecycle check (idle 60 min / lifetime 4 h / ended) → one-in-flight lock → idempotency by clientTurnId
  server: append buyer turn (conversationVersion+1)
  agent:  load_context → retrieve_knowledge (≤6 records) → model (≤3 calls, ≤2 repairs, ≤1 escalation)
  agent:  action = ask | propose | explain | answer | unsupported | refuse
  tools:  publishScenario = validate → BEGIN IMMEDIATE save → COMMIT → independent readback (list + detail)
  server: append tailor turns + story in one transaction → TurnResponse
```

Code, never the model, enforces: cookie ownership, session lifecycle, schema, counts/sizes, single root, parent linkage, timing containment, `ERROR ⇔ error`, detection only on `ERROR`, `outcomeKind` vs. error spans, root output = trace output, fictional hosts only (`*.example`, `*.test`, `*.invalid`, `localhost`), no executable content, `expectedVersion` precondition, atomic publication and readback before any success claim. Persisted IDs are derived by code: trace `${sessionId}-${traceKey}`, span `${sessionId}-${traceKey}-${spanKey}`; `ingestedAt` is the server clock.

## Outcome states (distinct, tested)

| `PublishResult.state` / `TurnOutcome` | Meaning | Buyer-facing rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `committed` | Saved and independently read back | May say "saved"; cite `evidence.traceIds/spanIds/version` from the readback |
| `rejected` | Validator refused after bounded repairs; nothing written (verified by re-read) | Say what was invalid; "last good version N is still live" |
| `save_failed` | Write failed, known unchanged | Same as rejected, with the reason |
| `readback_uncertain` | Transaction may have committed, readback failed | Say uncertain; never "unchanged" or "saved"; UI re-reads before next action |
| `conflict` | `expectedVersion` ≠ current | Nothing written; re-read and retry |
| `unsupported` | Outside clone capabilities | Explain-only or unknown; no fabricated feature |
| `refused` | Injection, arbitrary code, cross-session, real-product mutation | Short refusal, state unchanged |
| `expired` | Idle/lifetime/End demo | Access removed; conversation and demo data deleted |
| `clarification` | One material ambiguity | One question, exactly three relevant choices, free text allowed |
| `provider_unavailable` | Provider failed within budget | Nothing written |

## Example journey (travel booking)

1. Buyer: "I'm building a travel-booking agent. Show me a booking API timeout followed by a successful retry." → model returns `travelProposalV1` (`expectedVersion: 1`, `mode: 'new'`) → validator ok → save → readback returns version 2, trace `${sid}-booking-timeout-retry-ok`, 7 spans, 1 `ERROR` (`attempt-1`) → explanation cites those span IDs and the 2860 ms root.
2. Buyer: "Make the retry fail too." → `travelProposalV2` (`expectedVersion: 2`, `mode: 'edit'`) adds `booking-timeout-retry-fails` (2 `ERROR` spans, `attempt-2` is a detection, `outcomeKind: 'escalation'`) and makes it active; the v1 trace is carried over → version 3 → explanation names `attempt-1`, `attempt-2`, `escalate_to_travel_desk` and the `charged: false` output.
3. Failure examples: stale `expectedVersion` → `conflict`; a span whose parent is missing → `rejected` with `UNKNOWN_PARENT`; "delete the real Neatlogs project" → `refused`; "set up a Slack alert here" → `unsupported` (explain-only); "show me something failing" → `clarification`.

## Lifecycle

Server clock only (`Clock` is injectable for tests). Idle 60 minutes, lifetime 4 hours, explicit idempotent `POST /api/sessions/:id/end`. Reload within an active session restores the saved version. Expiry/end deletes the session row (conversation + dataset); a sweep every `LIMITS.sweepIntervalMs` removes sessions nobody revisits. Legacy seven-day cookies are treated as unknown sessions (404). No returning-buyer recognition.

## Conversation concurrency

Server appends turns; the client never replaces the transcript. `conversationVersion` increments per accepted append. One in-flight turn per session (`TURN_IN_FLIGHT` 409 for a second). Retrying the same `clientTurnId` returns the original response. History is bounded to 120 turns; older turns are trimmed server-side and `conversationTruncated` is set so the UI can say so.

## Telemetry

Real Tailor execution goes through `TurnTelemetry` (backend-owned exporter built on the pinned `neatlogs` SDK: `init`/`trace`/`span`, `disableExport`/caller-owned `tracerProvider` for the local captured exporter, `mask` for redaction). Synthetic demo traces never go there. Correlation IDs are opaque; raw buyer text, cookies and full payloads are not exported by default. Usage is recorded only when the provider reports it.

## Not in this snapshot

Provider/model IDs, money budgets, live telemetry destination approval, pricing facts (knowledge lane records them as known-with-source or unknown).

I notice Cursor saves transcripts to a nested subdirectory path, while Entire's integration looks for a flat file path instead, and that Cursor might only write the file at the end of a turn rather than during it—so for my own session the transcript location could follow that same nested pattern.

This looks like a real capture gap: the commit trailer gets created, but the checkpoint is skipped because there's no transcript at the expected path and seemingly no tracked file changes either, which is odd since file tracking shouldn't depend on the transcript existing. I shouldn't patch the hooks or fabricate data—I should just document this as a genuine mismatch between Cursor's actual transcript path/timing and what Entire expects, and I want to verify whether the earlier 4a4e0ead Cursor session actually produced checkpoints by checking the checkpoint list for that session.

I notice 4a4e0ead does have a metadata folder with a full.jsonl, meaning Entire successfully captured that session's transcript at some point—likely via the stop hook at turn end rather than at commit time. This suggests checkpoints for Cursor sessions may only form correctly if the transcript happens to be ready when the stop hook fires, which would explain the inconsistent capture behavior I'm seeing.

content.text:
I'm noticing that for session 4a4e0ead, checkpoints were saved on a shadow branch at turn stops with manual-commit strategy, and my own session should map to the shadow branch `entire/bbb2600-e3b0c4`, which does appear in the branch list — so checkpoints likely get saved at the end of each turn via the stop hook once the transcript is ready.

Since commit-time condensation was skipped because no session checkpoints existed yet, I'm realizing commit `f34adb3` references a checkpoint that may never materialize, meaning commits made mid-turn could structurally lack checkpoint objects in this harness. I plan to verify this once my turn ends to see if the pending checkpoint gets attached at the next stop.

This missing linkage is a verification gap, not a reason to amend the commit, so I'll flag it in the final report and move on to launching lanes. I'm weighing whether to end my turn early so the stop hook saves a session checkpoint before more commits pile up — launching the 4 background lanes now, giving an interim status to trigger Entire's stop hook, then letting subagent completion notifications wake me to continue gives both better capture and parallelism, though I'm unsure whether the harness actually resumes me reliably on background completion.

Since the tool description confirms I'll be notified automatically after ending my turn when a background agent finishes, that mechanism should work. But ending the turn after launching the lanes isn't really "stopping after planning" — it's a checkpoint report, though there's still a risk the notification doesn't fire and the user just sees a finished state. Given the user explicitly said they're not watching and the work must be delivered, I'll lean toward the blocking approach instead, doing everything within one turn and accepting that all commits made during that turn will lack checkpoint objects — a capture gap I'll need to report, while I think through whether there's a better alternative.

Live capture is clearly established — the session is active, hooks are firing, turn-start is logged, and the shadow session is initialized. The real gap is commit-time checkpoint materialization, not session-level capture, so per the ticket guidance I think continuing implementation is justified as long as that gap is reported honestly, perhaps with a background approach to narrow it further.

A better pattern emerges: run work in background lanes, end turns at natural milestones so stop hooks save session checkpoints, then commit at the start of the next turn once a prior checkpoint exists for condensation to use. The earlier commit f34adb3 was made mid-turn though, so that specific gap stays unresolved and should be noted as-is. I'm weighing the risk that background notifications might not arrive, but the tool explicitly promises them, so I'll proceed with that assumption.

Ending the turn here also gives the user a useful interim progress report, which fits the long-running nature of this task — I'll frame the interim message clearly as a status update saying lanes are running and I'll pick back up once they report.

Now I need to draft the lane prompts, making sure each is detailed and self-contained, starting with a shared preamble covering repo path, branch, baseline commit, and the key contract files each lane needs to read.

I'm also specifying the node rules and constraints each lane must follow: native TS conventions, import extension requirements, test invocation limited to node:test on owned files, and firm boundaries around git operations, secrets, installs, and network calls, plus a note that shared-checkout typecheck noise from other lanes should be ignored rather than fixed.

For the backend lane prompt specifically, I'm detailing what needs to happen in clock.ts (implementing the Clock type and systemClock, wiring it into the store) and validator.ts (building validateProposal to assemble a concrete Dataset with assigned IDs, carried-over traces in edit mode, synthetic tags, and ingestion timestamps).

I also need to handle validateDataset for the existing developer raw-proposal route, reusing structural checks like sessionId-prefixed IDs while keeping fixtures passing. Then for store.ts, I'm weighing schema changes — adding columns like expires_at, last_active_at, and state for sweep queries — and working out how session creation should behave before any dataset exists, since the current entry flow creates a session tied to a scenario but the new flow needs to handle the first turn differently.

For the entry page, I'm deciding that POST /api/sessions should create a session right away using the two regression fixtures as a starting "sample" dataset (activeScenario 'recovered', story null), so the UI always has traces to show. Then the agent processes the first message by proposing a 'new' dataset that replaces the fixtures, meaning buyers see sample traces until the dataset gets personalized to their input.

I'm also keeping the legacy `/api/sessions/:id/scenario` route available for regression testing even though the UI's agent-driven flow no longer calls it directly.

For the conversation-replace endpoint, I'm removing `POST /conversation` since the contract says clients never replace the transcript wholesale — the backend should own appends instead, which means updating the existing API test. I'm also sketching the new routes: turns, end, and session fetches that touch lastActiveAt and enforce expiry, returning a 410 SESSION_EXPIRED so the UI can render an expired state properly.

On expiry I'll delete the session row and run a sweep both on an interval in the server (unref'd) and opportunistically per-request. For turn orchestration, I'm working through the authorize → lifecycle check → in-memory per-session lock → idempotency flow, and realizing I need to persist the last turn response alongside lastClientTurnId so repeated submissions can return the cached result instead of just checking the id.

Then after appending the buyer turn, bumping the conversation version, and persisting, I call the agent's handleTurn, append the resulting messages/story transactionally, build and persist the TurnResponse, and return it -- with a fallback 'failed' tailor note if the agent throws. For session-tools.ts, publishScenario will validate, open an immediate transaction, re-read to confirm the expected version and active state, then update.

I'm designing the commit flow to do an independent readback through a separate read path after committing, reusing the same projection functions the HTTP GET endpoint uses, plus test hooks for simulating save or readback failures. I also need a conversation cap of 120 messages with oldest-trimming and a truncated flag, and a telemetry module that creates a telemetry instance with configurable modes (captured, disabled, neatlogs) exposing per-turn telemetry, flush, and snapshot functions.

For the captured mode, I'm working out how to wire neatlogs' init with a caller-owned tracer provider and disableExport set true, so spans route into an in-memory exporter instead of hitting the network, confirming that pairing a BasicTracerProvider with a SimpleSpanProcessor on that exporter lets neatlogs' trace/span calls land there correctly for tests.

I also need to make sure live telemetry only activates when TAILOR_TELEMETRY=neatlogs is explicitly set, never auto-loading env files, and that all telemetry calls are wrapped defensively with a bounded queue and non-blocking async init so nothing can break the demo. On redaction, I'm defining a mask function that strips sensitive fields like text, cookies, apiKey, description, and messages, keeping only an allowlist of safe attributes such as turnId, a hashed correlationId, outcome, step names, and durations.

For the trace call itself, I'm emitting a `tailor.turn` workflow span keyed by the correlationId with sanitized inputs, making sure init doesn't register shutdown handlers since we're not the owning provider, and confirming disableExport keeps things fully offline, verifiable via the local doctor check. Then I need to update the test suite, including API tests and a store test using a fake clock to cover idle timeout, lifetime expiry, idempotent session end, and reload/restart behavior.

I'm also planning out validator tests covering travel example migrations, fixture acceptance, and various malformed/invalid input cases, plus telemetry tests verifying redacted span capture and graceful exporter failure handling. For the turn route tests I'll stub out a minimal AgentService returning canned proposals rather than using the real agent, which should prove the route, tooling, and persistence layers work together, and I'll need to check whether the fixture script or README need updates to match.

For server wiring, I'm weighing how to compose the app server so it depends on an AgentService, provider, knowledge index, telemetry, and clock without creating a hard compile-time dependency on another lane's not-yet-written files -- the main entry point would import from the agent service, mock provider, and knowledge modules, but those imports would fail typecheck until those lanes are complete, so I need a way to structure this that avoids blocking on it.

I'll put the actual composition into a separate `src/main.ts`, owned by me as orchestrator and written only at integration time, keeping backend's server.ts limited to exporting `appServer` without a main block. I also need to update `npm run dev` and the Playwright webServer command to point at `src/main.ts`, both of which I own, while backend and agent lanes keep testing against stubs in the meantime -- though I'm now realizing the agent lane will need a live server to test the browser UI against while backend is simultaneously being rewritten, which is a real coordination problem.

Since the agent lane can't run the full integrated UI until integration happens, they should build the client against the contract types, write unit tests for the agent service against stub session tools, and mark Playwright as not-run until the integration wave. I'll skip having them build a separate dev harness to keep things simple, and instead draft the agent/UI lane prompt specifying the `createAgentService` function and its turn-handling logic.

Continuing that spec: the service enforces deterministic pre-checks even though the mock model decides actions, since prompt injection text must be treated as data. It builds context from a system prompt, a knowledge slice, session story, dataset summary, and recent turns, then calls the provider, parses the resulting action, and handles each case — starting with the "ask" action requiring exactly three clarification choices with a fallback if that check fails.

For "propose," rejected scenarios trigger repair attempts via another provider call (bounded by maxRepairs), while committed ones require an explanation grounded in deterministic readback evidence — spans, durations, errors — with the model's text serving only as narrative on top of that factual core. The "explain" action similarly reads back actual trace spans through tools.readTrace and composes a template-plus-narrative explanation from real span data rather than hallucinated details, and I'm now moving into how the "answer" action should stay grounded in the knowledge base.

I'm sketching the provider module next — a `createProvider` factory that reads the `TAILOR_PROVIDER` env var and defaults to the mock, with any live provider request throwing a clear "not configured" error so nothing unapproved gets pulled in. Then for the mock provider itself, I'm planning a deterministic heuristic that parses buyer text to infer domain and desired failure pattern like timeouts or retries.

I want to pass structured session context through a well-defined JSON block embedded in the user message rather than hacking it out of the system message, since both mock and live providers can consume that cleanly. Ambiguous requests should trigger a clarifying question with three concrete choices.

For knowledge questions, I'll answer only from the provided knowledge records and leave unknown pricing as unknown; injection, code execution, cross-session access, or real mutation attempts should be refused outright, and unsupported capabilities (alerts, Slack integration, replay) should return an unsupported response tagged with a capability id. The mock implementation must be clearly labeled as mock and avoid special-casing any particular domain like travel — extraction should stay generic.

Next I need to design the context assembly module with bounded scope, then rewrite the client's chat function to post turns to the session endpoint.

## What to build

### 1. Agent service — `src/agent/service.ts`
`export function createAgentService(): AgentService` implementing `handleTurn(input: AgentTurnInput): Promise<AgentTurnResult>` — ONE server-side product agent. The model (provider) interprets requests, asks clarifications, proposes bounded actions and narrates; CODE enforces budgets, grounding, and loop termination. Flow:
1. `load_context` (telemetry.step): resolve `choiceId` against the most recent tailor turn with `clarification` in `session.conversation` (map to the choice label as the effective buyer text; unknown choiceId -> treat text as free text). Build bounded context (`src/agent/context.ts`): story, dataset summary (per trace: key, label, outcome, outcomeKind, root duration, span names/status/kind, error strings — NOT full JSON), last 12 turns, unresolved question, dataset version, LIMITS. 2. `retrieve_knowledge`: `knowledge.select(text, LIMITS.maxKnowledgeRecordsPerTurn)`; include id/title/behaviour/limitations/demonstration.level/planAvailability in context.

Record `telemetry.recordUsage(response.usage, provider.model)` and latency. Budget: at most LIMITS.maxProviderCallsPerTurn calls, LIMITS.maxToolCallsPerTurn tool calls, LIMITS.maxRepairsPerTurn repairs. One optional escalation to `escalationProvider` (if present) after a failed repair, at most LIMITS.maxEscalationsPerTurn — record a TurnStep 'escalate'.
4. Act on the AgentAction:

   - `propose`: set `proposal.expectedVersion = session.version` if the model got it wrong? NO — pass through what the model returned; the backend decides `conflict`. Call `tools.publishScenario`. On `rejected` and repairs left: `repair` step, call provider again with `repairOf: problems`; else stop. On `committed`: build the grounded explanation in `src/agent/explain.ts` DETERMINISTICALLY from `readback` (version, trace label/ID, span count, root duration, error span IDs and names from `tools.readTrace(evidence.traceIds[0])`) and append the model's `explanation` narrative only after the evidence sentence. Attach `evidence` to the tailor turn. Outcome 'committed', buyer turn -> 'applied'. On `conflict`/`save_failed`/`readback_uncertain`/`expired`/`unsupported`: map 1:1 to TurnOutcome with truthful copy: never say "unchanged" unless the result state guarantees it (rejected/save_failed/conflict do; readback_uncertain does NOT — say the save may have gone through and the next view will show the real version).
   - `explain`: `tools.readTrace(traceId ?? active trace)`; explanation from ACTUAL spans (names, statuses, error text, timing offsets, outcome) — never from the scenario name alone. Attach evidence {version, traceIds, spanIds}.
   - `answer`: knowledge-grounded; cite record titles; if planAvailability is unknown say so plainly; outcome 'answered'.
   - `unsupported` / `refuse`: outcomes 'unsupported' / 'refused', state unchanged (no tool writes).
   - Provider throws or returns unparsable action after budget -> 'provider_unavailable', nothing written.
5. Return `execution: { mode: provider.mode, provider: provider.name, model: provider.model }`, `steps` with measured durations, `messages` (tailor turns only; the backend appends the buyer turn itself), `story` when committed.

### 2. Provider abstraction — `src/agent/provider.ts` + `src/agent/mock-provider.ts`

Set `expectedVersion` from the context's dataset version and `contractVersion`. Follow-ups like "make the retry fail too" must preserve names/inputs/timings of the existing active trace and only change the relevant spans/outcome (outcomeKind escalation or failure, detection on the exhausted attempt). Use `src/examples/travel-booking.ts` as the SHAPE reference only.
  - Explain: "explain/why/what happened/walk me through" -> `explain` with the active trace.
  - Answer: knowledge questions ("what does Neatlogs cost", "can it detect…") -> `answer` citing knowledge ids from context; unknown pricing stays unknown.

  - usage: null (mock does not report tokens; never fabricate), latencyMs measured.

### 3. Buyer UI — `src/client.ts`, `public/style.css`, `public/index.html`

'sample workflow'}`; scenario filter options come from the dataset's traces (key -> label); the notice becomes `Synthetic demo · Powered by Tailor · v${version} · ${activeLabel}`; remove `ADAPTER_LABEL` and all "Deterministic prototype adapter" / "Two fixtures" copy.
- Entry flow: first buyer message -> `POST /api/sessions` {description: text, conversation: []} with Idempotency-Key (reuse the existing operation/idempotency sessionStorage logic) -> navigate to `/demo/:id/traces` -> immediately `POST /turns` with that text as the first turn (same clientTurnId retry semantics). Draft in sessionStorage stays for the pre-session state only.
- Turn flow: `POST /api/sessions/:id/turns` {text, clientTurnId: crypto.randomUUID(), choiceId?}; show the buyer turn as Pending immediately; disable composer while in flight; on response APPEND `messages` (replace the optimistic buyer turn by id if the server echoes it, else keep it with the status implied by outcome); render `steps` as a compact progress line ("Checked context · Validated · Saved · Read back ✓"); render `clarification` as three buttons + the free-text composer; statuses: Pending/Applied/Failed/Uncertain/Question. On 'committed' re-fetch the session and trace list and only then repaint (never claim agreement before reading). On 'readback_uncertain' show an amber note and re-fetch. On 409 TURN_IN_FLIGHT show a small note "Still working on your last message". Retrying a failed network request reuses the same clientTurnId.
- Honest labels: a persistent small line under the panel header: `Powered by Tailor · synthetic data` and, when `execution.mode === 'mock'`, `Mock-backed prototype — no live model yet`. Never display hidden reasoning, provider payloads or credentials. Keep internal jargon (adapter, fixture, readback) out of buyer copy — say "saved and verified" etc.
- End demo: a button in the panel header -> `POST /api/sessions/:id/end` -> clear sessionStorage keys -> go to `/entry` with a one-line notice "Demo ended. Your conversation and demo data were deleted." Handle 410 SESSION_EXPIRED/SESSION_ENDED anywhere (render an "This demo has ended" screen with a link to start a new one; clear local state). Reload within an active session restores the saved version (already works via GET; keep it).
- Transcript bound: if `conversationTruncated` is true show "Older messages were trimmed" at the top of the thread.
- Accessibility/responsiveness as today (≤390px no horizontal scroll). Keep the existing CSS tokens; add minimal styles for steps, choices, uncertain state, End demo, ended screen.
- Delete `src/adapter.ts` and `test/adapter.test.ts`; update `tsconfig.browser.json` include accordingly (client + contracts + agent-contract types). The server's `/adapter.js` mapping may remain and 404 — fine.

### 4. Tests — `test/agent.test.ts` (+ `test/helpers/agent.ts`)

Fake `KnowledgeIndex` with 3–4 records (one explain_only e.g. alerts, one unknown pricing). No-op `TurnTelemetry` that records step names. Table of every URL fetched (URL, date, what it supports, fetch status), the list of topics you could NOT verify and therefore excluded or downgraded, and the known limits of this knowledge slice. Keep it factual.

# NIT-269 handoff — personalised Tailor agent proof

Branch `work/nit-269-build-personalised-tailor-agent-proof`, built on `main` at `bbb2600`. Nothing has been merged into `main` or deployed; both remain approval gates. This document states what works, what is mock-backed, what has not been verified, and what needs explicit approval. Test evidence with exact counts lives in [`nit-269-evidence.md`](nit-269-evidence.md); the seam is documented in [`nit-269-contract.md`](nit-269-contract.md); knowledge provenance in [`nit-269-knowledge-sources.md`](nit-269-knowledge-sources.md).

## Run it

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev            # build the browser bundle, then node src/main.ts on http://127.0.0.1:4321
```

`src/main.ts` is the composition root. It reads plain environment variables only and never loads `.env.local`:

| Variable | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | `4321` | Loopback only. |
| `TAILOR_DATA_PATH` | `.local/tailor.sqlite` | SQLite with WAL; directory created 0700. |
| `TAILOR_PROVIDER` | `mock` | Anything else exits with code 2. A live provider is an approval gate (see below). |
| `TAILOR_TELEMETRY` | `captured` | `disabled` (no-op), `captured` (in-memory, bounded), `neatlogs` (exports via the pinned SDK; exits 2 unless `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set in the shell). |
| `TAILOR_DEV_KEY` | unset | Enables `/api/dev/*` inspection routes. |
| `NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT` | SDK default | Only read in `neatlogs` mode. |

Gates: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:ui` (Playwright starts its own server on port 4322 with a throwaway database).

## What works (verified locally, mock provider)

- A buyer describes the agent they are building in the Neatlogs-styled entry page; one server-side agent interprets the request, proposes a `ScenarioProposal`, deterministic code validates it, saves it in one SQLite transaction, reads it back independently, and the reply cites only spans that exist in the read-back trace. The demo then shows the personalised trace in the list, detail, graph and timeline views.
- Follow-up edits ("Make the retry fail too.") keep the earlier trace, add the new one, and switch the active scenario; the reply explains what changed using the read-back evidence.
- Ambiguous requests get one clarification question with exactly three choices plus free text; choosing one resolves the turn. No company-name questionnaire.
- Explanations of the open trace ("Explain this trace") come from the saved spans, not from the model's memory of what it proposed.
- Questions about Neatlogs are answered from the versioned records in `knowledge/neatlogs/` (20 records, version `2026-10-11.1`). Official product claims are separated from what this clone can demonstrate. Pricing and plan availability are reported as unknown because they were not verified; hackathon access is not treated as proof of ordinary plan availability. Requests for features outside the records return `unsupported` with the dataset unchanged.
- Hostile input (prompt injection, requests to run code, to read another session, or to change the real Neatlogs project) is refused with the dataset version unchanged. Buyer text is HTML-escaped in the client.
- Sessions: HttpOnly, SameSite cookie bound to one session; 60 minutes idle or 4 hours total, whichever comes first, enforced on the server clock; expiry deletes the content and answers 410; **End demo** deletes immediately, clears the cookie, and leaves a content-free tombstone for 10 minutes; a sweeper runs every 5 minutes. Cross-session access answers 404 so existence is not leaked. No returning-buyer recognition.
- Reload restores the conversation from the server. Retrying the same `clientTurnId` returns the original response without a new version; a second concurrent turn on the same session gets 409 `TURN_IN_FLIGHT`. Conversations are capped at 120 turns and marked truncated rather than silently dropped.
- Save failure reports `save_failed` and says nothing changed only when the authoritative version really is unchanged; readback failure reports `readback_uncertain` and never claims success. Both paths are covered by injected faults.
- Runtime telemetry wraps the pinned Neatlogs SDK (`neatlogs@1.1.28`, `init`/`trace`/`span`/`flush`/`shutdown`, no invented endpoints or attributes). Each turn is a `WORKFLOW` trace with child spans for load_context, retrieve_knowledge, model, validate, save, readback and explain, carrying real latency, an HMAC-derived correlation ID (never the session ID), and allowlisted `tailor.*` attributes. Raw buyer text, cookies, descriptions and model/tool payloads are never attached. Exporter failures are counted in diagnostics and never fail a turn. Token usage is recorded only when a provider reports it; nothing is estimated.

## What is mock-backed

- `TAILOR_PROVIDER=mock` is the only provider. The mock (`src/agent/mock-provider.ts`) is heuristic: it recognises a bounded set of domains and failure shapes, so "unfamiliar wording" works to the extent the heuristics cover it. The UI labels this honestly ("Mock-backed prototype — no live model yet"); nothing pretends to be a live model.
- Because the provider is mock, model-quality claims (interpretation of arbitrary wording, proposal richness, explanation prose) are **not** verified. Everything deterministic around the model — validation, permissions, schemas, relationships, timing, session ownership, version checks, save/readback, lifecycle, telemetry shape — is verified and is model-free.
- The eval set (`docs/nit-269-eval-set.json`) measures the mock, not a model.

## Not verified / not run

- **External Neatlogs ingestion.** `TAILOR_TELEMETRY=neatlogs` is implemented against the official SDK contract and tested only with the local captured exporter. No trace from this branch has been sent to or looked up in a Neatlogs project. Running it needs the key in the shell environment (not `.env.local`), confirmation of the Tailor Neatlogs project and region, and your approval. The synthetic demo traces the buyer sees live only in SQLite and are never exported; Tailor's own runtime telemetry is what `neatlogs` mode would export.
- **Live model behaviour.** No live model call has been made and no charge incurred. `createProvider({ kind: 'live' })` throws until a provider/model is approved and configured.
- **Deployment.** Not attempted; no credentials created or configured.

## Approval gates (explicit, in order of likely need)

1. Live provider: provider and model ID, data-flow statement (buyer text leaves the machine), API eligibility, spend cap. Then wire it in `src/agent/provider.ts` behind `TAILOR_PROVIDER`.
2. External telemetry: Tailor Neatlogs project and region confirmed; key present in the shell; run `TAILOR_TELEMETRY=neatlogs npm run dev`, send a turn, and look the trace up by its correlation ID in that project before claiming ingestion works.
3. Merge into `main` and any deployment.

## Known limits

- The in-flight lock is per process; running more than one server process against the same SQLite file is not supported.
- Knowledge retrieval is keyword-bounded (`KnowledgeIndex.select`), deliberately without a vector store; records are small enough to fit the model context in full.
- Entire capture: commits on this branch carry hook-added `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers where the hook assigned one; see the Linear report for which checkpoint refs materialised. Missing refs are a capture gap to report, not something to repair by rewriting history.

## File map

| Area | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Contract | `src/agent-contract.ts`, `src/contracts.ts`, `src/examples/travel-booking.ts`, `docs/nit-269-contract.md` |
| Backend | `src/store.ts`, `src/server.ts`, `src/validator.ts`, `src/session-tools.ts`, `src/telemetry.ts`, `src/fixtures.ts` |
| Agent and UI | `src/agent/*`, `src/client.ts`, `public/style.css`, `src/main.ts` |
| Knowledge | `knowledge/README.md`, `knowledge/neatlogs/*.json`, `src/knowledge.ts` |
| Tests | `test/*.test.ts` (node:test), `ui/*.spec.ts` (Playwright) |

content.text:
I'm routing to the agent lane and setting instructions for building product answers strictly from cited records—pulling title, behavior summary, limitations, plan availability, and source details—while stripping out any unverified pricing or plan claims from the model's prose.

Medium priority: for committed/explain narratives, I want a grounding function that drops sentences referencing identifier-like tokens (span names, UUIDs, trace IDs) not found in the actual read-back trace, or that make unverified claims about real mutations like "saved" or "deleted." I'm also planning test coverage in agent.test.ts to validate this filtering logic.

For CROSS_SESSION detection, I'm adding patterns to catch session IDs, UUIDs near words like "session" or "trace," and phrasing like "show session <id>" or paths like "/demo/<id>" — while being careful not to flag legitimate references to "this session" without an actual identifier.

I'll have the lane run typecheck and tests without committing, since I'll handle the commit myself, and dispatch this in the background — the edits here (src/agent and test/agent files) are disjoint from QA wave 2's test-file-only changes, so there's no conflict.


I've confirmed the reviewer's three findings in the code: `actOnAnswer` prepends unchecked model prose, `describeCommit`/`actOnExplain` append unchecked narrative, and `CROSS_SESSION` fails to match identifiers. Since these all live in the agent lane's files, I'll route the fix there along with the review's evidence.

arguments.prompt:
Wave 2 defect fixes for NIT-272. Integration is on branch work/nit-269-build-personalised-tailor-agent-proof (HEAD 34eeb76, tree clean; all gates green: typecheck, npm test 96/96, build, test:ui 6/6). An independent security/grounding review (gpt-5.6) found three real defects in your lane's files. Fix them. File ownership unchanged: edit only `src/agent/*`, `test/agent.test.ts`, `test/helpers/agent.ts` (and `src/client.ts`/`public/style.css` only if strictly needed — not expected). Do NOT touch `src/agent-contract.ts`, `src/server.ts`, `src/store.ts`, `src/validator.ts`, `src/knowledge.ts`, `knowledge/`, `test/qa-*.ts`, `ui/*`, docs. Do not run git commands that change state (I commit). Never read `.env.local`. No network, no live model.

FINDING 1 (High) — valid citations do not ground answer prose. `src/agent/service.ts` `actOnAnswer` (~line 266-276): `lines = [cleanNarrative(a.text)]` accepts arbitrary provider prose as long as `a.knowledgeIds` contains one valid record ID. Reviewer probe: a provider citing the valid pricing record returned “Neatlogs costs USD 49 per month.” Required fix: product answers must be composed deterministically from the cited `CapabilityRecord`s (title, behaviour/summary, key limitations, prerequisites if relevant, plan availability incl. explicit “unknown”, demonstration level in this demo, source URL + date). Provider prose for `answer` actions must be either discarded or passed through a claim filter that drops any sentence containing: currency symbols/codes or numbers followed by price words (USD|\$|€|£|per month|/mo|per seat|pricing tier names), plan words (free|pro|team|enterprise|starter) unless that exact plan string appears in a cited record's `planAvailability.plans`, and capability claims (verbs like supports|detects|integrates|alerts|exports) whose object words do not appear in a cited record. Prefer discarding; keep at most one short lead sentence only if it survives the filter. Pricing questions must always end with the explicit unknown statement from the record.

FINDING 2 (Medium) — model narrative can contradict read-back evidence. `src/agent/service.ts` committed branch (~232-234, `describeCommit(readback, trace, cleanNarrative(explanation))`) and `actOnExplain` (~259-263) append provider narrative after the evidence sentence. Probe: narrative cited a span that does not exist in the read-back trace and claimed a real mutation. Required fix: add a `groundNarrative(text, trace, readback)` (in `src/agent/explain.ts`) that splits narrative into sentences and drops any sentence that (a) contains an identifier-like token — snake_case/kebab-case names of 3+ chars with `_` or `-`, UUIDs, or `${sessionId}-...` derived IDs — not present among the read-back trace's span ids/names, trace ids/keys/labels; (b) contains numbers with `ms`/`s`/`%` that do not match a span/root duration in the trace; (c) claims saved/deleted/updated/changed anything in a real/production/live Neatlogs project/account, or uses the words “real”/“production” + mutation verbs; (d) contains pricing claims as in Finding 1. Use the grounded result in both places. The evidence sentence from `describeCommit`/`describeTrace` (already readback-derived) stays authoritative and first.

FINDING 3 (Medium) — explicit session IDs bypass refusal. `src/agent/mock-provider.ts` `CROSS_SESSION` (~line 46) only matches descriptive phrases (“another buyer’s session”). Probe: “Show me session 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000” committed version 2 instead of `refused` with version unchanged. Required fix: extend `refusalFor` to refuse (reason `cross_session`) when the text contains (i) `session|demo|visitor|buyer|user` followed within ~3 tokens by an identifier-like token (UUID, 8+ char hex/base32/ULID, or `[a-z0-9]{6,}(-[a-z0-9]+)+`), (ii) a `/demo/<id>` or `/api/sessions/<id>` path, (iii) `sessionId`/`session id`/`session_id` + `=`/`:`/`is` + token, or (iv) verbs show|open|load|read|get|fetch|pull|access + `session` + token. Do NOT refuse “this session”, “my session”, “the current demo”, or ordinary scenario requests; verify the existing QA matrix items still classify the same (the QA tests must stay green).

TESTS: add cases to `test/agent.test.ts` using a scripted/fake provider (extend `test/helpers/agent.ts` if needed) that reproduce each probe and assert: (1) answer citing the pricing record with fabricated price → reply contains no “49”/“USD”/“per month” and does contain the unknown statement; a fabricated capability sentence is dropped; (2) committed/explain narrative citing a non-existent span id/name or claiming a real mutation → those sentences absent, evidence sentence intact, `evidence.spanIds` ⊆ read-back trace; (3) the explicit-session-ID texts → outcome `refused`, version unchanged; plus negative cases (“explain this session’s trace” still works).

Run `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (all, including QA matrix) and `npm run test:ui` from the repo root before reporting; all must be green. Return as your final message: files changed, a one-paragraph description of each fix, the new test names, and exact gate counts.

I see now that the commit explanation currently comes from the proposal action's first call, grounded by groundNarrative. What's needed instead is a two-call flow: one planning call, then a separate evidence-grounded explanation call using the read-back trace as evidence, with its narrative also grounded. For mock mode, I'm thinking the mock provider could handle a cheap 'explanation' response schema request.

I'm leaning toward adding an optional `explain` method on the ModelProvider interface, keyed to an evidence-based request/response contract, so the live provider can implement it while the mock provider falls back to using the proposal's existing explanation — keeping backwards compatibility. I also need to extend ProviderUsage with optional cache token fields, noting that thinking tokens aren't separately reported by Anthropic (they're folded into output tokens), so I'll document that limitation rather than invent a field that doesn't exist.

Cost estimates should live in the spend ledger and dev logs rather than in telemetry usage, since telemetry should only reflect provider-reported numbers — I'll label any estimate clearly as an estimate that may differ from final billing.

For the contract file, I'll own those changes myself as orchestrator, then split implementation into lanes: the agent lane handles the live Anthropic provider, the spend guard/ledger, provider factory wiring, explanation prompts, JSON schema validation, error mapping, and offline tests using a fake fetch/SDK, plus pinning the Anthropic SDK dependency.

I'll own the main.ts wiring, env vars, and .env.example, and for .env.local I need to be careful not to read or print its contents — I'll use a count-only grep check to detect whether ANTHROPIC_API_KEY already exists, consistent with the sanctioned env:check approach rather than catting the file directly.

Given the risk of duplicating keys with a blind append, the safer path is to instruct the user to manually add the line themselves, while I extend env:check so it safely reports set/missing status without reading values. I'll also note docs, package.json scripts, and a small telemetry change to recordUsage to include extended usage fields.

For parallelizing work: I'll handle the contract, main.ts, env/scripts/docs, and telemetry usage fields; the agent lane covers the provider, spend logic, service explanation call, and unit tests; and QA can independently build the spend-guard/error matrix tests plus a live smoke script that exercises the running server end-to-end and prints usage/cost, gated behind the API key and spend cap.

To let both lanes work without guessing at interfaces, I need to nail down the contract first, specifically the shape of provider usage data covering input/output tokens plus optional cache read/creation token counts, since thinking tokens get folded into output tokens rather than tracked separately.

I'm also defining the explanation request/response types: a request carrying the message history and schema name for evidence explanations, and a response pairing the explanation text with span IDs, usage, and latency. I'm sketching the ModelProvider interface with an optional explain method for the post-save readback step, which absent providers like the mock can simply skip.

I need an error taxonomy for providers — a union type covering things like auth failures, rate limits, timeouts, and malformed responses — plus a ProviderError class carrying the kind, retryability, and an optional request ID. I'm deciding to keep the error kind type in the shared contract file but put the actual error class in the provider module itself, since the contract file is types-only.

The service layer then maps these provider errors to telemetry events and a generic 'provider_unavailable' outcome, with internal details (like auth or spend-cap issues) only surfaced in operator-facing step details and telemetry, never in buyer-facing copy. I'm also adding an optional effort field to ExecutionLabel, skipping escalation provider wiring since the baseline has no escalation, and setting a 30-second model timeout for the live Sonnet call at medium effort.

Actually a 30s timeout seems too tight — a proposal's JSON output could take close to 25s alone at typical token rates, leaving little margin for thinking time. I should make this configurable instead, adding a `providerTimeoutMs` field (around 60s) to LIMITS in the contract, and have the lane consume that value. Time to write out the contract changes now.
