Ownership: you edit `src/agent/**` and `test/agent*.ts`, `test/helpers/agent.ts` only. Do NOT edit `src/agent-contract.ts` (ask me if you need a contract change), `src/main.ts`, `src/server.ts`, `src/store.ts`, `src/telemetry.ts`, `package.json`, `.env*`, docs, `ui/*`, `test/qa-*`. No git state changes. NEVER read `.env.local`, never print or log any env var value, never make a network call: all tests must be offline with an injected fake client. Do not add dependencies (no zod).

VERIFIED FACTS (from current official Anthropic docs — use these, do not copy older patterns): model id `claude-sonnet-5-5` ($2 input / $10 output per MTok); adaptive thinking is the default — send `thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }` (display defaults to omitted); `thinking.type 'disabled'` and `enabled/budget_tokens` return 400 on this model — never send them; effort is `output_config.effort: 'medium'` (also accepts low/high/xhigh/max); structured JSON output is `output_config.format` via `client.messages.parse({...})` with `jsonSchemaOutputFormat(schema)` from `@anthropic-ai/sdk/helpers/json-schema` (GA, no beta header); schema rules: every object `additionalProperties: false`, all properties listed in `required`, no minimum/maximum/minLength/maxLength/pattern (unsupported — the helper strips some but keep the schema clean), enums and nested objects/arrays are fine; `parsed_output` is null when the text is not valid JSON (e.g. refusal). Response: `stop_reason` in `end_turn | max_tokens | refusal | model_context_window_exceeded | tool_use | pause_turn | stop_sequence`; refusal is HTTP 200 with `stop_details {type:'refusal', category|null, explanation|null}`; `usage: { input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens|null, cache_read_input_tokens|null, output_tokens_details: { thinking_tokens } | null }` — thinking tokens are inside output_tokens; `_request_id` on the response. SDK client options `apiKey`, `maxRetries` (default 2, retries 429/5xx/connection with backoff), `timeout` (ms). SDK error classes: `Anthropic.AuthenticationError` (401), `PermissionDeniedError` (403), `BadRequestError` (400 — also returned when an org/workspace spend limit is reached; a 402 billing error surfaces as `APIError` status 402), `RateLimitError` (429), `InternalServerError` (5xx incl. 529 overloaded), `APIConnectionTimeoutError`, `APIConnectionError`, `APIUserAbortError`. We do NOT use tools/tool_choice: the model returns one structured AgentAction and OUR server executes it.

CONTRACT (read `src/agent-contract.ts`): `ModelProvider { name; model; mode; effort?; complete(ProviderRequest, signal) -> ProviderResponse; explain?(ExplanationRequest, signal) -> ExplanationResponse }`; `ProviderUsage` now has optional `cacheReadInputTokens`, `cacheCreationInputTokens`, `thinkingTokens`; `ProviderResponse.requestId?`; `ProviderErrorKind` union; `LIMITS.maxExplanationOutputTokens = 800`, `LIMITS.providerTimeoutMs = 60000`, `LIMITS.maxInputCharsPerCall = 60000`; `ExecutionLabel.effort?`.

DELIVERABLES
1. `src/agent/anthropic-provider.ts` — `createAnthropicProvider(options: { apiKey: string; model?: string (default 'claude-sonnet-5-5'); effort?: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'xhigh'|'max' (default 'medium'); maxRetries?: number (default 2); timeoutMs?: number (default LIMITS.providerTimeoutMs); spend: SpendGuard; client?: MessagesClientLike /* injectable for tests: { messages: { parse(params): Promise<ParsedMessage> } } */ }): ModelProvider`. `complete()` builds `{ model, max_tokens: min(request.maxOutputTokens, LIMITS.maxOutputTokens), system: <system message content>, messages: <user/assistant turns mapped; 'tool' role mapped to a user message prefixed as untrusted tool data>, thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }, output_config: { effort, format: jsonSchemaOutputFormat(AGENT_ACTION_SCHEMA) } }` and calls `client.messages.parse(params, { signal })`. Reject before calling if total prompt chars > LIMITS.maxInputCharsPerCall (throw ProviderError 'invalid_request'). `explain()` does the same with `EVIDENCE_EXPLANATION_SCHEMA` and `LIMITS.maxExplanationOutputTokens`. Map results: `stop_reason === 'refusal'` → throw `ProviderError('refusal')` (include stop_details.category in the message, never buyer text); `max_tokens` or `model_context_window_exceeded` → 'truncated'/'context_exceeded'; `parsed_output` null or failing `validateAgentAction` → 'malformed'; SDK errors → auth/permission/billing(402)/spend_cap(400 whose message mentions spend/limit)/invalid_request(other 400)/rate_limit/overloaded(529)/timeout/network/unknown. Always convert usage to ProviderUsage (nullable cache fields → undefined, thinking from output_tokens_details) and call `spend.record(usage, model, kind)` BEFORE throwing on refusal/truncation (those are billed). Export `class ProviderError extends Error { kind: ProviderErrorKind; retryable: boolean; requestId?: string; status?: number }` (no parameter properties — erasableSyntaxOnly). Export the two JSON schemas as plain `as const` objects; the AgentAction schema must mirror the `AgentAction` union exactly (discriminated by `type`; use `anyOf` of 6 objects; ScenarioProposal/ProposedTrace/ProposedSpan fields incl. `kind`, `contractVersion`, `expectedVersion`, `mode`, `removeTraceKeys`, `story{domain,summary,assumptions}`, `activeScenario`, `traces[]{key,label,outcomeKind,outcome,input,output,tags,spans[]{key,parentKey(string|null),name,kind(enum SPAN_KINDS),startMs,durationMs,status(enum OK/ERROR),input,output,error(string|null),detection(string|null)}}` — check `ProposedSpan/ProposedTrace` in the contract for exact field names/optionality; where a field is optional in TS, make it `type: [..., 'null']` and required in the schema (structured outputs require all properties listed) and normalise null→undefined before `validateAgentAction`). `input`/`output` are free-form JSON: declare them as `{ type: 'string' }` carrying a JSON string if the structured-output grammar can’t express arbitrary JSON, and parse+`isJson` them server-side (bounded by LIMITS.maxSpanJsonBytes); document the choice.
2. `src/agent/spend.ts` — `createSpendGuard({ capUsd: number; rates: { inputPerMTok: 2, outputPerMTok: 10, cacheReadPerMTok?: 0.2, cacheWritePerMTok?: 2.5 } (defaults for claude-sonnet-5-5; configurable); ledgerPath?: string /* .local/spend-ledger.json, persisted atomically so restarts keep the running total */; clock?; perCallMaxOutputTokens: LIMITS.maxOutputTokens; perTurnMaxCalls: LIMITS.maxProviderCallsPerTurn }): SpendGuard` with `check(estimatedMaxUsdForThisCall)` (throws ProviderError 'spend_cap' when `spentUsd + estimated > capUsd`; estimate the worst case for the call from prompt chars/4 input tokens + max_tokens output), `record(usage, model, kind)`, `summary(): { capUsd, spentUsd (estimated from reported usage × rates), calls, inputTokens, outputTokens, thinkingTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, byKind }`. Label every USD number `estimated`; the summary must say local estimates may differ from final Anthropic billing. Never write secrets to the ledger.
3. `src/agent/provider.ts` — `ProviderConfig = { kind: 'mock' } | { kind: 'anthropic'; apiKey: string; model?: string; effort?: Effort; spend: SpendGuard; maxRetries?; timeoutMs?; client? }`; `createProvider` dispatches; keep `validateAgentAction`, `parseAgentAction`, `isJson` exports; add `validateEvidenceExplanation(value): EvidenceExplanation | null`. Remove the old 'live throws' branch.
4. `src/agent/service.ts` — after a COMMITTED publish and the read-back `tools.readTrace`, if `provider.explain` exists call it ONCE (counts toward providerCalls, bounded by the same budget, uses `step('explain', ...)` and `telemetry.recordUsage`) with messages = system prompt for explanation + user message containing: the buyer’s request text (as untrusted quoted data), the proposal story, and the READ-BACK evidence (trace label/outcome, each span id/name/kind/status/duration/error — from the trace we read back, never from the proposal) — build it in `src/agent/prompts.ts` as `explanationMessage(...)`; result passes through `groundNarrative` against the read-back trace exactly like today and replaces the planning explanation; `evidence.spanIds` must be ⊆ read-back span ids (fallback to error spans). If `explain` throws or is absent, fall back to the planning explanation (grounded) and record a telemetry event `explain_unavailable` with the error kind — the turn stays `committed`. Make `MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS` = `LIMITS.providerTimeoutMs`. On `ProviderError` from the planning call, record `provider_error` with `kind` and set the failed step detail to a short operator-safe string (e.g. 'auth', 'rate_limit', 'spend_cap'); the buyer-facing `provider_unavailable` copy stays generic, except `spend_cap`, which should say the demo’s model budget for today is used up (no numbers). NEVER fall back to the mock in live mode. Keep `ExecutionLabel.effort` populated from `provider.effort`.
5. Mock provider: unchanged behaviour; expose `effort: null`.
6. Tests (`test/agent.test.ts` or a new `test/anthropic-provider.test.ts` under your ownership) using an injected fake `client.messages.parse`: (a) request shape — model, `thinking.type === 'adaptive'`, no `budget_tokens`, no `disabled`, `output_config.effort === 'medium'`, `output_config.format.type === 'json_schema'`, `max_tokens` bounded, system/user mapping, prompt-size rejection; (b) success path maps usage incl. cache + thinking fields and `requestId`; (c) refusal → ProviderError 'refusal' and usage recorded; (d) max_tokens → 'truncated'; (e) parsed_output null / schema-invalid action → 'malformed'; (f) SDK errors → auth/rate_limit/overloaded/timeout/network/spend_cap/billing mapping and `retryable` flags; (g) spend guard: cap enforcement before the call, ledger persistence across two guard instances (tmp dir), summary math; (h) service: committed turn with a provider that has `explain` makes exactly 2 provider calls, explanation grounded, spanIds ⊆ read-back; explain failure keeps `committed` with fallback text; planning auth error → `provider_unavailable` with step detail 'auth' and no mock fallback; (i) schema self-check: `validateAgentAction` accepts the example proposals in `src/examples/travel-booking.ts` round-tripped through the schema’s null/optional normalisation.
Run `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` (all green) before reporting. Report: files, how `input/output` JSON is represented in the schema, the exact request params object for a planning call (redacted of content), test names, gate counts, and anything in the contract you needed but lacked.

New QA task (NIT-271 extension): the live Anthropic provider is being implemented in parallel by the agent lane (files `src/agent/anthropic-provider.ts`, `src/agent/spend.ts`, changes in `src/agent/provider.ts`/`service.ts`). You own and may edit ONLY: `scripts/live-smoke.ts` (new), `test/qa-live-contract.test.ts` (new), `docs/nit-269-eval-set.json`, `docs/nit-269-evidence.md`. No git state changes; never read `.env.local`; never print env var values; no network from tests. Verified Anthropic facts you can rely on: model `claude-sonnet-5-5`, adaptive thinking default, `output_config.effort: 'medium'`, structured output via `output_config.format`, `stop_reason` refusal/max_tokens/model_context_window_exceeded, usage has `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`; thinking tokens are inside output_tokens. Contract: see `src/agent-contract.ts` (`ModelProvider.explain?`, `ProviderUsage` cache/thinking fields, `ProviderErrorKind`, `LIMITS.providerTimeoutMs`, `TurnResponse.execution { mode, provider, model, effort }`).

Deliverable A — `scripts/live-smoke.ts`: a script run as `node --env-file-if-exists=.env.local scripts/live-smoke.ts` AGAINST AN ALREADY RUNNING server (`TAILOR_URL`, default http://127.0.0.1:4321), that performs the approved live test sequence over HTTP only: (1) POST /api/sessions (Idempotency-Key, description 'Live smoke — invented travel-booking buyer'); (2) turn: “I’m building a travel-booking agent. Show me a booking API timeout followed by a successful retry.” → expect outcome committed, version 2, evidence present; (3) turn: “Make the retry fail too.” → committed, version 3, two traces retained, active trace has 2 ERROR spans; (4) GET session + traces + each trace detail + one span: assert list/detail/span agree and that every span id cited in the explanation evidence exists in the saved trace; GET the session again (reload consistency: conversation and version unchanged); (5) turn: “Show me something failing.” → expect clarification with exactly 3 choices, then answer with choiceId; (6) turn requesting an unsupported feature (e.g. “Set up Slack alerts for this project”) → unsupported, version unchanged; (7) POST /end. For every turn print: outcome, version, execution.{mode,provider,model,effort}, steps with status/duration, and the buyer-facing text; never print cookies. At the end GET `/api/dev/spend` IF it exists (I am adding it in `src/server.ts`: returns the spend guard summary — estimated USD, calls, input/output/thinking/cache tokens; requires header `x-tailor-dev-key` from `TAILOR_DEV_KEY` env) and print it, labelling all USD as estimated and noting Anthropic billing may differ; if the route is absent, say so. The script must refuse to run if `execution.mode` of the first turn is not `live` when `TAILOR_EXPECT_LIVE=1` (so we never mistake a mock run for a live verification), exit non-zero on any assertion failure, and print a final PASS/FAIL table. Use invented data only; the script must not read any env var other than TAILOR_URL, TAILOR_DEV_KEY, TAILOR_EXPECT_LIVE and must never read or print ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

Deliverable B — `test/qa-live-contract.test.ts` (offline, node:test): black-box tests against the agent service + a scripted FAKE provider implementing `ModelProvider` (incl. `explain`) that assert the service-level behaviour the live baseline must have regardless of the provider internals: (1) a provider whose `complete` throws an Error named 'ProviderError' with `kind: 'auth'` → TurnResponse outcome `provider_unavailable`, dataset version unchanged, `execution.mode === 'live'` (as reported by the fake), and the reply never contains the words mock/fallback; (2) kinds rate_limit, timeout, overloaded, spend_cap → `provider_unavailable`, version unchanged (spend_cap copy mentions budget but no numbers); (3) `complete` resolves a valid propose action and `explain` resolves text citing one real span and one fabricated span id → outcome committed, reply drops the fabricated id, `evidence.spanIds` ⊆ read-back spans, exactly 2 provider calls; (4) `explain` throws → still committed with grounded fallback explanation; (5) a propose that fails validation twice → `rejected` with ≤3 provider calls; (6) usage from the fake with cache + thinking fields reaches telemetry (`telemetry.captured()` attributes) without any buyer text. Use the same harness composition as `test/qa-journey.test.ts` (Store with tmp sqlite, `createTelemetry({mode:'captured'})`, `createAgentService()`, `appServer(store, {...})`, pass your fake as `provider`). Where the service hasn’t landed the explain step yet when you run, write the tests to the contract and mark the ones that fail with a clear message; I will run them again after integration.

Deliverable C — update `docs/nit-269-evidence.md` with a new 'Live provider (pending key + cap)' section: what the smoke script checks, that NO live call has been made yet, and the exact fields that will be reported (model, effort, provider usage incl. thinking/cache, estimated USD). Run `npm run typecheck` and your test file; report file list, test names, pass/fail counts, and anything in the contract or routes you had to assume.

<available_subagent_types>
Available subagent_types and a quick description of what they do:
- generalPurpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. Use when searching for a keyword or file and not confident you'll find the match quickly.
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- browser-use: Perform browser-based testing and web automation. This subagent can navigate web pages, interact with elements, fill forms, and take screenshots. Use this for testing web applications, verifying UI changes, or any browser-based tasks. Use this browser subagent when you need to either: (1) parallelize browser tasks alongside other work, or (2) execute a longer sequence of browser actions that benefit from dedicated context. For simple, single browser actions, you may use the browser tools directly. This subagent requires agent mode because browser MCP access is unavailable in readonly mode. This subagent_type is stateful; if a browserUse subagent already exists, the previously created subagent will be resumed if you reuse the Task tool with subagent_type set to browserUse. (Auto-resumes most recent agent of this type; `resume` arg is ignored)
- cursor-guide: Read Cursor product documentation to answer questions about how Cursor Desktop, IDE, CLI, Cloud Agents, Bugbot, and other features work. Use when the user asks 'In Cursor, how do I...?' or similar questions about Cursor products.
- ci-investigator: Investigate a single failing PR CI check and return a short root-cause summary. Use when the user asks to summarize, explain, diagnose, or investigate a specific failed check from a pull request.
- bugbot: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a Bugbot-like review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Bugbot". Launch exactly one Bugbot subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\", \"natural language\">\nChange Description: ...\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Change Description` only when `Diff` is `natural language`, formatting it as one block per changed file (a `<path> (added|modified|deleted|renamed)` header followed by bullets of what changed, mentioning line numbers or ranges inline where helpful), and only use `natural language` as a last resort after a regular diff-based review failed because the diff could not be computed; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- security-review: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a security review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Security Review". Launch exactly one security-review subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\">\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- best-of-n-runner: Run a task in an isolated git worktree. Each best-of-n-runner gets its own branch and working directory. Use for best-of-N parallel attempts or isolated experiments.
- ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications.
- deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline.
- performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance.
</available_subagent_types>

<available_subagent_models>
If the user explicitly asks for the model of a subagent/task, you may ONLY use model slugs from this list:
- inherit (default; required unless the user explicitly requested another model)
- claude-fable-5-1-thinking-high
- claude-opus-5-5-medium
- claude-sonnet-5-5-high
- composer-2.5-fast
- cursor-grok-4.6-medium-fast
- gemini-3.8-flash-high
- gpt-5.6-sol-medium
- grok-4.7-high-fast
- muse-spark-1.3-high

If the user isn't asking for a specific version, prefer the latest version of the model family. As an example, if the user just says "gpt" or "claude", use the latest available version of GPT or Claude.

IMPORTANT: If the user requests a model that is NOT in the list above, do NOT substitute a different model or guess. Instead, skip launching the subagent with that model and tell the user which model was unavailable and which models are available.

When speaking to the USER about which model you selected for a subagent, do NOT use the kebab-case model names unless the user requested the model using that format. Ue the same naming scheme the user used to discuss the model when they requested it.
</available_subagent_models>

<dynamic_tool_catalog>
These dynamic tool namespaces were available when this conversation started. Availability may have changed, so use `GetDynamicTools` to check current state before calling `CallDynamicTool`.

<dynamic_tool_namespaces>
<namespace name="cursor-origin" tools="get_repository, list_repositories, list_namespaces, create_repository, get_file_contents, get_git_tree, grep_contents, list_branches, list_commits, commit_read, compare_commits, sync_mirror, list_pull_requests, pull_request_read, create_pull_request, update_pull_request, update_pull_request_base, merge_pull_request, create_pull_request_review, update_pull_request_review, dismiss_pull_request_review, create_pull_request_comment, create_pull_request_inline_comment, reply_pull_request_review_thread, update_pull_request_review_thread, update_pull_request_comment, update_pull_request_labels, create_label, request_pull_request_reviewers, remove_pull_request_reviewers, checks_read" namespaceUseInstructions="Cursor Origin (origin.cursor.com) is a git host. These tools only see repositories hosted on Origin, addressed by their Origin namespace (owner) and repository name. A repository that only mirrors to Origin still counts as Origin-hosted. Repositories on GitHub or any other host are not visible here, so do not pass a GitHub owner or repository name; call list_namespaces to find the owners the caller can use." source="mcp" />
<namespace name="cursor-ide-browser" tools="browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_click, browser_mouse_click_xy, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, browser_drag, browser_get_bounding_box, browser_highlight, browser_tabs, browser_cdp, browser_take_screenshot, browser_lock" namespaceUseInstructions="The cursor-ide-browser MCP server provides a Cursor-owned browser tab plus a raw Chrome DevTools Protocol command tool.

CORE WORKFLOW:
1. Start by understanding the user's goal and what success looks like on the page.
2. Use browser_tabs with action "list" to inspect open tabs and URLs before acting.
3. Use browser_navigate to create or navigate the target tab. Omit the position parameter for background automation so focus is preserved.
4. Use browser_lock before longer automation on an existing tab, then browser_lock with action "unlock" when finished.
5. Use browser_snapshot for accessibility context and browser_take_screenshot for visual verification.
6. Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for page interactions.
7. Use browser_highlight and browser_get_bounding_box for visual grounding and coordinate diagnostics.
8. Use browser_cdp for page inspection, profiling, runtime evaluation, DOM/CSS queries, and performance data.

AVOID RABBIT HOLES:
1. Do not repeat the same failing action more than once without new evidence such as a fresh snapshot, a different ref, a changed page state, or a clear new hypothesis.
2. IMPORTANT: If four attempts fail or progress stalls, stop acting and report what you observed, what blocked progress, and the most likely next step.
3. Prefer gathering evidence over brute force. If the page is confusing, use browser_snapshot, browser_take_screenshot, or CDP inspection before trying more actions.
4. If you encounter a blocker such as login, passkey/manual user interaction, permissions, captchas, destructive confirmations, missing data, or an unexpected state, stop and report it instead of improvising repeated actions.
5. Do not get stuck in wait-action-wait loops. Every retry should be justified by something newly observed.

CRITICAL - Lock/unlock workflow:
1. browser_lock requires an existing browser tab - you CANNOT call browser_lock with action: "lock" before browser_navigate
2. Correct order: browser_navigate -> browser_lock({ action: "lock" }) -> (interactions) -> browser_lock({ action: "unlock" })
3. If a browser tab already exists (check with browser_tabs list), call browser_lock with action: "lock" FIRST before any interactions
4. Only call browser_lock with action: "unlock" when completely done with ALL browser operations for this turn

IMPORTANT - Waiting strategy:
When waiting for page changes, prefer short CDP polling loops with Runtime.evaluate, DOM queries, Page lifecycle signals, or browser_snapshot checks rather than a single long wait.

CDP USAGE:
- Use browser_cdp with a DevTools Protocol method and params object, for example Runtime.evaluate, DOM.getDocument, CSS.getComputedStyleForNode, Profiler.start/stop, Performance.getMetrics, Log.enable, and Network.enable.
- Do not use browser_cdp with CDP Input.* methods. They are denied because they are focus-sensitive in Electron webviews and can route input to Cursor UI instead of the browser page.
- Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for clicks, typing, filling inputs, selecting options, keyboard actions, scrolling, and drag-and-drop.
- Use Runtime.evaluate for advanced DOM-scoped interactions that the dedicated browser tools do not cover.
- For profiling, call Profiler.enable, Profiler.start, reproduce the behavior, then Profiler.stop. The profile is saved to a file and returned as a log_file; read that file only when you need to inspect details.
- For JavaScript evaluation, prefer Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue when possible.
- Device emulation you set with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled, or Emulation.setUserAgentOverride (for example for a phone-sized screenshot) lasts only for the current turn: it is cleared when your turn ends, and the user can reset it from the browser tab at any time. Send Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride yourself once you are done with it within a turn.
- Some browser-wide or sensitive CDP methods are denied, especially cookie, storage, permission, download, target-management, filesystem-backed file-input commands, system-level commands, and CDP navigation/history navigation commands.
- Large CDP responses are saved to files instead of being inlined. Prefer using the returned file path over immediately stuffing large payloads into context; read focused sections only when needed.

VISION:
- browser_take_screenshot attaches an image result that the model can inspect. CDP Page.captureScreenshot returns data inside JSON and should not replace browser_take_screenshot when visual verification is needed.

NOTES:
- browser_snapshot returns snapshot YAML and is the main source of truth for page structure.
- Refs are opaque handles tied to the latest browser_snapshot for that tab.
- Iframe content is not accessible - only elements outside iframes can be interacted with.
- When you stop to report a blocker, include the current page, the target you were trying to reach, the blocker you observed, and the best next action. If the blocker requires manual user interaction, ask the user to take over at that point rather than assuming it in advance." source="mcp" />
<namespace name="plugin-paper-desktop-paper" tools="open_file, list_resources, create_file, rename_resource, create_page, rename_pages, get_basic_info, get_selection, get_node_info, get_children, get_screenshot, get_jsx, get_tree_summary, get_computed_styles, get_fill_image, find_nodes, list_comment_threads, get_comment_thread, list_comment_thread_authors, set_comment_thread_status, get_font_family_info, get_guide, export, export_combined_pdf, write_html, create_artboard, delete_nodes, set_text_content, rename_nodes, update_styles, duplicate_nodes, move_nodes, finish_working_on_nodes, get_tokens, create_tokens, set_tokens" namespaceUseInstructions="Paper is a professional design tool for creating user interfaces. The user is working on a 2D canvas composing designs.
The Paper MCP server gives you tools to be a talented designer for web and mobile apps and websites. You can read designs from the user's file, see what the user is doing, and write HTML back into the design as new nodes.

You MUST load the full guide before other Paper tools: get_guide({ topic: "paper-mcp-instructions" }). Do this once per session; call again if a long thread may have dropped guide text.

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

# Copy to .env.local (gitignored, chmod 600) or export in your shell. Never commit real values.
# Scripts that need secrets run `node --env-file-if-exists=.env.local …`; shell-exported variables win over this file.

# ---- Neatlogs (Tailor runtime telemetry) -------------------------------------------------------
# Project key. Only needed for `neatlogs doctor --probe`, `npm run smoke:trace` and TAILOR_TELEMETRY=neatlogs.
NEATLOGS_API_KEY=
# Ingest base URL. Default is US; EU projects use https://eu.ingest.neatlogs.com
NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT=https://ingest.neatlogs.com

# ---- Anthropic (live Tailor agent; approval-gated) ---------------------------------------------
# Server-side API key from the Anthropic Console project "tailor-neathack". Enter it here yourself.
# Read only by `npm run dev:live`; never printed, logged, exported through telemetry or sent anywhere but api.anthropic.com.
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
# Numeric USD cap for live calls, approved by you before any paid call. The server refuses to start in live mode without it.
# The guard works from provider-reported usage × list rates; estimates can differ from final Anthropic billing.
TAILOR_LIVE_CAP_USD=
# Baseline model and effort (verified against current Anthropic docs; adaptive thinking is the model default).
TAILOR_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5
TAILOR_EFFORT=medium

# ---- Local developer inspection (not secret, local only) ---------------------------------------
# Enables GET /api/dev/sessions and GET /api/dev/spend with header x-tailor-dev-key.
TAILOR_DEV_KEY=

Knowledge retrieval, permissions, schema/timing/relationship validation, persistence, version checks and read-back stay in deterministic code; model output is validated structurally and grounded before use. Refusals (`stop_reason: refusal`), truncation (`max_tokens`), malformed output, 401/403/402, 429, 529, timeouts and network errors are mapped to a `ProviderErrorKind`, recorded in telemetry and surfaced to the buyer as a generic "nothing changed" reply.

content.text:
The live Anthropic provider is implemented, verified against the real API under your $5 cap, committed and pushed to the existing feature branch (`8dd4b9d`, local = remote). `main` untouched, nothing deployed.

## What ran live

- **Model/effort as requested:** every turn's execution label read `mode=live · provider=anthropic · model=claude-sonnet-5-5 · effort=medium`; adaptive thinking (model default), structured JSON via `output_config.format`, no tools — all verified against current Anthropic docs before coding.
- **Scripted journey, 8/8 PASS:** travel booking timeout → successful retry (committed v2); "make the retry fail too" (committed v3, both traces retained, 2 ERROR spans); list/detail/span agreement, cited span ids exist, reload consistent; fresh-session clarification with exactly 3 choices + free text, then choice → committed; "Set up Slack alerts" → `unsupported`, version unchanged; end session; spend summary.
- **Browser check** on the live server: "Powered by Tailor · synthetic data" (no mock label), turn Applied, "Evidence · v2 · open trace · 4 steps cited".
- **Call shape:** every committed turn is exactly 2 model calls — plan (~10–15 s) + evidence-grounded explain from the read-back (~3 s). The explanations name real saved span keys and durations, and the deterministic "Saved and verified as version N…" prefix comes from the independent readback.

## Found and fixed by the first live calls

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Every turn `provider_unavailable` / `invalid_request` | API 400 "compiled grammar is too large" — six-way `anyOf` | Flat schema discriminated by `type`; server rebuilds the union |
| Same 400 after the fix | SDK `jsonSchemaOutputFormat` default transform demotes every `enum` to a description | `transform: false`; test pins the wire schema |
| Edit replaced the first trace | Prompt never stated edit semantics (mock had them hard-coded) | Prompt rule: keep traces, add variation as new active trace |
| Repair call on every edit | "Story exceeds 600 characters" | Prompt states the combined limit |

Also added opt-in `TAILOR_PROVIDER_DEBUG=1` (logs the API's own error type/message only). Importantly: on failure, live mode did exactly what you asked — a generic "nothing changed" reply, no mock fallback, zero usage recorded.

## Usage and estimated cost

Provider-reported, cumulative across all runs including the failing ones: **43 calls** (28 plan / 15 explain), **267,696 input / 48,297 output tokens, of which 8,985 thinking**, 0 cache read/write (no prompt caching configured). **Est. $1.02 of the $5 cap** at list rates, plus ≈$0.02 for four direct SDK schema probes outside the guard. ≈$0.03 per committed turn, ≈$0.02 per clarification/unsupported turn. These are local estimates from reported usage × list rates; your Anthropic Console is authoritative and may differ.

## Tests

- Passed: typecheck; `npm test` 148/148 (incl. 27 provider tests, 6 live-contract tests); build; Playwright 6/6 (mock); live smoke 8/8.
- Not run live (offline tests only): refusal, truncation, 401/403/402, 429, 529, timeout, spend-cap trip.
- **Hosted Neatlogs ingestion: not verified.** Live runs used the local captured exporter; no Tailor span, usage attribute or buyer/model content left the machine for Neatlogs. That stays a separate approval.

## Running it yourself

- Key location: `.env.local` in the repo root (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=`; already set per `npm run env:check`, value never read). Cap: either `TAILOR_LIVE_CAP_USD=5` in `.env.local` or on the command line.
- Start: `TAILOR_LIVE_CAP_USD=5 REDACTED npm run dev:live` → `http://127.0.0.1:4321/entry`. Note: a stale `node src/server.ts` from Saturday night (PID 50622) still holds 4321; I did not kill it. Use `PORT=4323 …` → `http://127.0.0.1:4323/entry` or stop that process.
- Checklist: send the travel prompt → "Make the retry fail too" → reload → in a fresh session "Show me something failing." then pick a choice → "Set up Slack alerts for this project." → `npm run smoke:live` (with `TAILOR_URL`, `TAILOR_DEV_KEY`, `TAILOR_EXPECT_LIVE=1`) for the scripted version. Full checklist is in `docs/nit-269-handoff.md`.
- I stopped my live server so there's no unattended paid surface.

## Entire

4 of this phase's 6 commits carry checkpoint trailers whose refs match locally and on origin (21 refs both sides, this session's ID, correct `files_touched`). `97f377b` and `8dd4b9d` have no trailer — the hook logged "transcript file not ready / session skipped" again. Nothing amended.
